kpis.sub: FROM POST-IPO HIGH, DESPITE A LOCKUP RALLY

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Confirmed Aug 5 that the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion traced to the main oxygen valve on a BE-4 engine; second-stage hot fires continue at NASA Stennis' B-2 stand as Launch Complex 36 repairs proceed. NASA's Isaacman says New Glenn remains "Plan A" for an Mk 1 launch before year-end.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Reports Q2 2026 results Aug 11, fresh off a $144M NASA CLPS contract for a 2028 Blue Ghost lunar mission and onboarding to a $981M U.S. Space Force IDIQ (Jul 31); analyst median price target $41 despite recent share weakness.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Extended its Series D to $860M (adding $350M in February), bringing total raised to $1.34B; completed Nova Stage 1 proto-qualification testing in early June; first Nova liftoff from Cape Canaveral's LC-14 still targeted for end of 2026.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space's Series D alone has grown to $1.34B raised before its first launch; dilution is chronic among small caps (RKLB's Iridium roll-up, ASTS's $1B convertible notes).

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — SDA's Golden Dome build-out alone is driving billions in LHX/Sierra Space awards; budget shifts or program cancellations reprice backlogs fast.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — even SpaceX itself needed a 92% revenue surge and improving Starlink economics just to narrow its Q2 net loss to $541M, and shares are still down ~41% from their post-IPO high despite that beat; xAI's AI cash burn continues to weigh on consolidated results.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed landing or launch can halve a small-cap (see lunar-lander names); Blue Origin's own May 28 pad explosion and this week's root-cause finding (a single oxygen valve) show how fast hardware failure can set a program back months. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Backlog swelled to ~$2.2B on a fresh $663M in Space Force awards that gave still-unflown Neutron its first confirmed defense mission (due 2028), and the ~$8B Iridium roll-up remains the clearest path to profitable, recurring cash flow in the sector; Q2 results land after today's close, so treat the current setup as guidance, not fact.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Space payloads and communications on prime-contractor economics remain the way to own the sector without owning a pre-revenue story; the $955M Golden Dome Tranche 3 award (part of a $1.75B round with Sierra Space) keeps that backlog growing. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count the exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Upgraded from Speculative: Q2 revenue hit a record $117.1M (+89.6% YoY), gross margin turned positive and record at 27.8%, and backlog reached $542.1M on a 1.42 book-to-bill — the proven-revenue bar for Core is now met, even though the company is still far smaller and less diversified than RKLB or LHX.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: The successful Aug 5 BlueBird 11-13 launch and reaffirmed $150-200M 2026 guidance are real progress, but the $1B convertible note overhang and a valuation still priced for a constellation that isn't fully built keep this speculative, not core.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Milestone-funded lunar programmes stay politically fragile and binary; assembling a third Nova-C lander for IM-3 is progress, not proof, and Q2 results (Aug 13) haven't landed yet.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Q2 revenue beat by 92% YoY and Starlink logged its best subscriber quarter ever (12M, ARPU steady at $66), but at a $1.75T market cap, still down ~41% from its post-IPO high, with lockup tranches unlocking on a rolling basis through Dec 8, 2026 and xAI's cash burn blurring the picture, the entry price is the open question, not the business. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Downgraded from Speculative: no fresh evidence this week to justify holding capital in a name whose central question — whether earth-observation data commands a defensible price — remains as open as it was last quarter; this week's gains came on sector beta, not company news.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Now effectively a merger-arbitrage position pending Rocket Lab's ~$8B acquisition (targeted close mid-2027, consideration collared $67.50-$112.50 of RKLB stock plus $27 cash); deal-completion and financing risk over that timeline isn't the same risk/reward as owning a satcom operator outright — RKLB stock is the cleaner way to take the same view.
